title: A hymn in Kanara
hookLine: Guru Arjan's hymn of a person with no enemy and no stranger, and how he got there

cards: The person at the next table. The driver. A name scrolling past in the comments.
Not disliked, exactly; just not counted yet. That's what a stranger is. A hymn of Guru Arjan in Raga Kanara says, in plain English: no one is my enemy, no one is a stranger.
It's a big thing for anyone to say, and the second half asks more than the first. The hymn says that whole category has emptied out. And it tells you how.

teach.b: Here's the hymn, in paraphrase, in its own order. It begins with what went missing: I have forgotten all my jealousy of others, ever since I found the company of the holy.
Then the line we started with: no one is my enemy, no one is a stranger; I get along with everyone.

teach.h: WHATEVER GOD DOES, ACCEPTED AS GOOD.
teach.b: Then: whatever God does, I accept as good; this wisdom I received from the holy.

teach.h: THE ONE IN ALL; NANAK BLOSSOMS.
teach.b: And it ends: the One God is present in all, and seeing this, Nanak blossoms. The order is building something. First, jealousy goes, the quiet engine behind a lot of distance between people: comparing, keeping score.
With it gone, enemies are harder to keep. Then strangers go too, because the last line explains why nobody is foreign anymore: the same One is present in every one of them.
And the source of all of it is named twice: the company of the holy. That's yesterday's thread, picked up in the same raga.
Guru Ram Das's mind turned green in good company; in Guru Arjan's hymn, that same company empties out jealousy, enemies and strangers.
The word for stranger here is bigana, an outsider, someone who isn't one of yours. The hymn doesn't say strangers stop existing. It says that from where this person stands, there aren't any left.
And the closing image isn't a rule but a flowering: seeing the One in everyone, Nanak blossoms. Your line: no stranger.

how: Guru Arjan's Kanara hymn is sung in kirtan in gurdwaras and at home, in Raga Kanara.

games.q: what does “a hymn in kanara” mean?
o: Guru Arjan's song: no one is an enemy, no one a stranger
Guru Arjan's warning to keep well away from strangers
a hymn asking God to defeat every last enemy

games.q: what's inside the hymn — tap the pairs.

s: the hymn says strangers stop existing
it says that, from where this person stands, no one is a stranger anymore.
the hymn names the company of the holy as the source
jealousy is forgotten, and wisdom is received, in that company.
the hymn ends with a rule about how to treat people
it ends with a flowering: seeing the One in all, Nanak blossoms.

games.q: in Guru Arjan's hymn, what goes first, before enemies and strangers disappear?
games.why: the hymn opens: I have forgotten all my jealousy of others, since I found the company of the holy.

practice: If you can, play this hymn or another shabad sung in Kanara, or sit in the quiet, and bring to mind someone you passed today without really seeing: a cashier, a neighbor, a face on a screen.
Let them stand in front of you for a few breaths, with a morning, a family and a worry of their own, and let them stop being background.
If you pray, hold the hymn's last thought, that the One is present in them too; if you don't, simply let them count.

wordCard.voice: A hymn in Kanara. Guru Arjan's song of forgetting jealousy in the company of the holy, until no one is an enemy, no one a stranger, and the One is seen in all. Today's word.

orig.note: bigana: a stranger, an outsider; the hymn says no one is one.

carryVoice: Your line: no stranger. In Guru Arjan's hymn, it all starts with forgetting jealousy. See you tomorrow.
